abstract: We construct an explicit smooth projective genus-21 curve arising from the regular-twin Diophantine construction with anchors $a=10783710$ and $b=-3/(4a)$. The curve includes the original cyclic cubic lift, rather than only its diagonal quotient. It has a point over every completion of $\mathbb Q$ but no rational point. This provides a concrete failure of the Hasse principle in a regular-sixth-entry construction. The global obstruction comes from a necessary intersection of two diagonal quadrics: its rational points would map to an elliptic curve of rank zero and full rational two-torsion, whose four rational points all have impossible inverse fibers. Exact algebraic rank and torsion computations, integer square bounds, and projective boundary checks certify the exclusion. Local solubility is proved at every place using explicit witnesses at small and nonunit-anchor primes, neighborhoods of poles at primes splitting in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, and a uniform Hasse–Weil argument at large inert primes. Three norm identities show that all relevant branch discriminants and resultants remain nonzero at those inert primes, so no unexamined bad reductions remain. Independently written certificates verify the signed square identities, branch data, arithmetic obstruction, and all finite witnesses. The result demonstrates a genuine global obstruction that cannot be resolved by further local existence tests. It concerns this specific regular-sixth candidate and does not decide arbitrary extensions or rational Diophantine septuple existence.

coauthors.contribution: Developed the necessary elliptic quotient and rank-zero obstruction, corrected signed local tests, supplied split-prime and local witness arguments, and independently audited all finite inputs and the complete all-place/projective proof.

title: A Hasse-principle failure on a fully lifted regular-twin Diophantine curve
